restoration_note: This teaching describes how the archons (Saklas/Nebroel and their powers), seeing the image of the Third Ambassador revealed in the cosmos, mold Adam and Eve as a counterfeit imitation of the divine likeness — the self organizing a humanity 'according to the image of the Most High' but only in likeness, not in truth. The doctrinal frame is the parable of the noble woman in her chamber: the Lord shows his image not for the crowding archons but for the soul who is his beloved. Restoration was tightly constrained in (a) recurring formulas — 'manifest the image forth,' 'according to his likeness,' 'God is intent in heart,' the 'Adam and Eve' pairing — which the editor's proposals consistently capture; and (b) Greek loanwords (ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ, ⲉⲝⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ, ⲡⲟⲗⲓⲥ, ⲕⲟⲓⲧⲱⲛ, ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ, ⲡⲉⲧⲣⲁ, ⲙⲉⲅⲓⲥⲧⲁⲛⲟⲥ) whose letter-completions are mechanical. The middle of the parable (lines 44–66, the chamber description, the brother whom no one has seen, the woman's coming and going) and the 'three moldings' coda (lines 116, 126, 133, 138) suffered from substantial multi-word lacunae with no parallel formula to anchor them; these were marked unrestorable. Editor's proposed ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ for {118} 'the male' was accepted with moderate confidence as the 'male and his female' archonic pair fits the Manichaean seduction motif, though the lexeme is unusual. The third-molding section's identification of the boundary-Father, the Adamas of Light subduing the Enthumesis of Death, and the standing-fast of the Adamas at the cisterns of the north — these passages were preserved enough that key spiritual anchors hold even where minor letters are restored.
